# `isolation-tax` — CLI reference

**Generated by running `--help` on the installed tool.** Regenerate with
`python oss/tools/gen_docs.py`. A hand-written reference drifts the moment a flag
changes, and a drifted reference is a confident description of software that no
longer exists.

## Top level

```
usage: isolation-tax [-h] [--version] {measure,fleet,demo} ...

what does per-tenant KV-cache isolation cost you?

positional arguments:
  {measure,fleet,demo}
    measure             measure the tax on a JSONL trace
    fleet               price the measured tax as GPU-equivalents and annual
                        dollars
    demo                a worked example, exact vs bounded

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --version             show program's version number and exit
```

## `isolation-tax measure`

```
usage: isolation-tax measure [-h] [--json] [--tok-per-s TOK_PER_S]
                             [--fail-over FRAC]
                             trace

positional arguments:
  trace                 path to a JSONL trace, or - for stdin

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --json
  --tok-per-s TOK_PER_S
                        assumed generation rate for the timing constraint
                        (BOUNDED mode only). Faster = weaker constraint = more
                        conservative floor.
  --fail-over FRAC      exit 1 if the tax exceeds this fraction of cache
                        benefit (e.g. 0.20)
```

## `isolation-tax fleet`

```
usage: isolation-tax fleet [-h] [--gpu GPU]
                           [--model-weights-gb MODEL_WEIGHTS_GB]
                           [--gpu-memory-gb GPU_MEMORY_GB]
                           [--gpu-usd-hr GPU_USD_HR]
                           [--kv-bytes-per-token KV_BYTES_PER_TOKEN]
                           [--layers LAYERS] [--kv-heads KV_HEADS]
                           [--head-dim HEAD_DIM] [--dtype-bytes DTYPE_BYTES]
                           [--fleet-gpus FLEET_GPUS] [--reserve-gb RESERVE_GB]
                           [--utilisation UTILISATION]
                           [--session-bound-fraction SESSION_BOUND_FRACTION]
                           [--kv-fill KV_FILL] [--tok-per-s TOK_PER_S]
                           [--json] [--fail-over-usd USD]
                           trace

Turn the measured hit count into GPUs and an annual dollar RANGE. The range is
not hedging: the conversion factor was MEASURED to vary 0.879-0.954 across
three models on one A100, nothing predicts where yours lands, and a point
estimate would be a false precision in a financial figure. Outside that
measured envelope -- another card, a model outside 0.99-29.54 GB of weights, a
KV pool that does not fill -- it ABSTAINS with exit 2 and names the axis,
rather than carrying a band measured elsewhere onto your fleet. NOT an end-to-
end serving benchmark: the one time this estate measured serving end to end it
got 0.997x. Every parameter below is REQUIRED and none is defaulted -- a
dollar figure from invented inputs is the failure this package exists to
catch.

positional arguments:
  trace                 path to a JSONL trace, or - for stdin

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --gpu GPU             the accelerator, as a label for the report (e.g.
                        A100-80GB)
  --model-weights-gb MODEL_WEIGHTS_GB
                        resident weight footprint PER GPU, in GB (1e9 bytes).
                        Use the sharded figure if the model runs tensor-
                        parallel.
  --gpu-memory-gb GPU_MEMORY_GB
                        HBM per GPU, in GB (1e9 bytes)
  --gpu-usd-hr GPU_USD_HR
                        your price per GPU-hour
  --kv-bytes-per-token KV_BYTES_PER_TOKEN
                        KV bytes per token. Or give --layers/--kv-
                        heads/--head-dim/--dtype-bytes and it is computed as
                        2*layers*kv_heads*head_dim*dtype_bytes.
  --layers LAYERS       model config: number of layers
  --kv-heads KV_HEADS   model config: KV heads (GQA groups, not Q heads)
  --head-dim HEAD_DIM   model config: head dimension
  --dtype-bytes DTYPE_BYTES
                        model config: KV dtype width (2 for fp16)
  --fleet-gpus FLEET_GPUS
                        GPUs you run today, under isolation
  --reserve-gb RESERVE_GB
                        activations + fragmentation headroom held back from
                        the KV pool (default 4, from the source capacity
                        model)
  --utilisation UTILISATION
                        ASSUMPTION: fraction of wall-clock hours billed
                        (default 1.0 = reserved capacity around the clock).
                        Not measured by anything here.
  --session-bound-fraction SESSION_BOUND_FRACTION
                        ASSUMPTION: fraction of the fleet whose capacity is
                        bound by the KV pool (default 1.0). Not measured by
                        anything here.
  --kv-fill KV_FILL     how full the KV pool runs, as a fraction of memory
                        left after weights and reserve. FIXED AT 1.0 by the
                        measurement -- both arms filled the card, which is the
                        comparison itself -- so any other value ABSTAINS
                        rather than scaling a band measured in a regime you
                        are not in.
  --tok-per-s TOK_PER_S
                        assumed generation rate for the timing constraint
                        (BOUNDED mode only)
  --json
  --fail-over-usd USD   exit 1 if the modelled annual cost exceeds this many
                        dollars
```
